decisive_items: multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum
several sessile, smooth-surfaced nodules (0.5–2 cm) in the pyloric antrum
Cytological brushing of the gastric mucosa demonstrated mucosal cells, mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation, and occasional large, non-septate hyphae with irregular diameter and branching
response.rationale: The champion candidate, C1, is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of multiple rounded echogenic neoformations and sessile nodules in the pyloric antrum, as well as the cytological findings of non-septate hyphae, which are consistent with basidiobolomycosis. The runner-up candidate, R5, is gastric neoplasia, but it is less likely due to the presence of non-septate hyphae, which are not typically seen in neoplastic lesions.

rejected.why: The candidate, R3, foodborne infection, is less likely due to the lack of evidence of bacterial or parasitic infection in the cytological brushing or other diagnostic tests.

The candidate, R2, gastrointestinal foreign body, is unlikely due to the absence of evidence of a foreign body on imaging studies and the presence of non-septate hyphae, which are not consistent with a foreign body.
The candidate, R6, gastrointestinal basidiobolomycosis, is similar to the champion candidate, C1, but it is less specific due to the lack of anatomical location (pyloric antrum) in the label.
